rootCause: auth.json was written in place (opened, truncated, written), so a full disk, a size limit or a killed process during the write left it empty or cut short. It is now replaced through a temporary file in the same directory (private from creation, fsynced, renamed over the file, directory flushed), so such a failure leaves the old file whole. The mode, the owner where the process may set it, and the extended attributes (the POSIX ACL on Linux, the user's attributes on macOS) where the file system takes them are kept; a symlinked auth.json is followed; on Windows ReplaceFileW keeps the replaced file's DACL. A read-only auth.json is refused as before. A file with more than one hard link, or whose extended attributes cannot be carried over, is written in place as before, as in Pi, and so are a single file mounted into a container, a file in a directory that cannot be written, and a device or named pipe.
reason: The root cause derives from the message of commit 4ec88b40bc, which is immutable. Its last sentence (a hard link and extended attributes on Unix are not carried over) has been false since 50164c1d6b: a file with more than one hard link is written in place, and extended attributes are carried over where the file system takes them (docs/parity/divergences/D651.md, TestWriteFileWritesInPlaceThroughAHardLink, TestWriteFileCarriesExtendedAttributesOver, TestWriteFileWritesInPlaceWhenAnAttributeCannotBeCarried). The text is the cause its changelog fragment states.

rootCause: When another process took auth.json's lock while a refresh was in flight (the sync lock goes stale after 10 s, a slow refresh outlasts it), Modify returned the compromise error and dropped the credential the refresh had obtained, which may have spent a single-use refresh token. While the lock's heartbeat has not yet reported the takeover, Modify now writes that provider's entry alone, under a lock of its own, into the file as it is then; what the other process wrote stays, and Pi persists the credential in that case. Once the heartbeat has reported the takeover, Modify still returns the lock error and writes nothing, as Pi throws. An fn that fails still writes nothing.
reason: The root cause derives from the message of commit 93b5de031b, which is immutable. It says Modify writes the provider's entry after any takeover; that has been false since 241a0a8c59, which keeps the lock error for a takeover the lock's heartbeat already reported (TestAuthStorageLockCompromisedDuringModifyUpstream runs Pi on it; TestAuthStorageModifierPersistsItsCredentialAfterTheLockWasTaken covers the unreported case). The text is the cause its changelog fragment states.
